scenes.title: What is a Cascode?
scenes.narration: A cascode is a two-transistor circuit designed to boost output impedance. By stacking devices, it helps create high-gain amplifiers or more ideal current sources.

scenes.title: How the Cascode Works
scenes.narration: The input device converts voltage to current, which then flows into a common-gate stage. This arrangement results in significantly higher impedance than a single transistor.

scenes.title: The Impedance Advantage
scenes.narration: Because the impedance at the source is divided by the device's gain and output resistance, the total output impedance increases to approximately gm multiplied by rO squared.

visual.formula_where: gm is transconductance, rO is output resistance
